Okay, I've just kicked off the salvage script in the background. The command I ran (`cat > /tmp/salvage_run.py ...`) launched a Python process (pid 1371707) that is executing the full benchmark/salvage pipeline: loading checkpoints, evaluating on the leaderboard, detecting the device, running benchmark and slerp phases, etc. This is a fairly heavy operation that can take several minutes, especially since it will run through the full training/evaluation loops on the GPU. I need to monitor its progress without blocking the main session, because I still have to keep the assistant responsive and possibly run other commands later.

The salvage script writes its log output to `/tmp/salvage.log` (I saw the script redirect its prints there). I should wait until the script reaches a point where it reports either the final "instruct results:" summary or any Traceback indicating a failure. Once that happens, I can fetch the relevant final lines (like final results, perplexity metrics, benchmark scores, or any errors) and present them to the user.

Since the script may take a while, I’ll use a background Bash loop that polls the log file every few minutes. The `until grep -qE "instruct results:|Traceback" /tmp/salvage.log; do sleep 180; done` construct will keep sleeping 180 seconds (3 minutes) until the log contains either of those markers. After the loop exits, I’ll echo a sentinel `SALVAGE_DONE` so I know the watch is finished, and then I’ll extract the last relevant lines from the log: replace any carriage returns with newlines (`tr '\r' '\n'`) and grep for key result patterns (`final results|byte perplexity|blimp|arc-easy|placement|Traceback|Error`), taking the last 10 lines to give a concise summary.

Running this as a background tool call (`run_in_background: true`) ensures the assistant can continue to respond while the monitoring happens. This aligns with the earlier steps: I killed the stray GPU processes, stashed foreign edits, verified tests pass, and now I'm salvaging the run to extract the final evaluation metrics. Monitoring the log is the next logical step before I can report the results back to the user.

Thus, the appropriate next action is to launch this background watch command.
